title: Monoidal local algebra criterion for regularity and parameter lifts
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $P$ be a fine saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively and sharp (its only invertible element is $0$). Let $a:P\to(A,\cdot)$ be a monoid homomorphism with $a(p)\in\mathfrak m$ for every $p\ne0$. For a monoid ideal $J\subseteq P$ (a subset with $J+P\subseteq J$, including the empty subset), put $JA=(a(j):j\in J)$, and assume $a^{-1}(JA)=J$ for every $J$. Put $I=(a(p):p\ne0)$ and $r=\dim_{\mathbf Q}(P^{\mathrm{gp}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q)$. Suppose $A/I$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] and $\dim A=\dim(A/I)+r$, where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then the set of indecomposable nonzero elements of $P$ is finite and generates $P$, and $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is torsion free. If these elements are enumerated without repetitions as $p_1,\ldots,p_n$, their images form a $k$-basis of $I/\mathfrak mI$. Moreover $A$ is regular local if and only if $n=r$, if and only if $P\cong\mathbf N^r$. If $P\cong\mathbf N^r$, write $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ for the images of its basis under $a$. For any regular system of parameters of $A/I$ and any lifts $b_1,\ldots,b_s\in\mathfrak m$ of that system, $(t_1,\ldots,t_r,b_1,\ldots,b_s)$ is a regular system of parameters of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. The cases $P=0$, $r=0$ and $s=0$ are included.

proof.text: Choose an inclusion-minimal finite monoid generating set $S$ of $P$, omitting $0$. Every indecomposable nonzero element belongs to $S$: in an expression as a sum of generators, two or more nonzero summands would decompose it. Conversely, if $s\in S$ were $x+y$ with $x,y\ne0$, express $x,y$ in $S$. An occurrence of $s$ would give $s=s+z+y$ (or the symmetric equality); cancellation and sharpness would force $y=0$ (or $x=0$). Thus neither expression contains $s$, contradicting minimality of $S$. Hence $S$ is exactly the finite set of indecomposables and generates $P$. Also, if $g\in P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ and $Ng=0$ for $N>0$, saturation puts both $g$ and $-g$ in $P$; sharpness gives $g=0$. Here cancellation and saturation are precisely the properties in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. This proves torsion freeness without a structure theorem for finitely generated groups.

proof.text:
Write $u_i=a(p_i)$. By step 1, every nonzero monomial is divisible by some $u_i$, so $I=(u_1,\ldots,u_n)$. Fix $i$ and let $J_i= igcup_{j
e i}(p_j+P)$. Indecomposability and distinctness imply $p_i
otin J_i$, even when $J_i$ is empty. Contraction therefore says $u_i
otin(u_j:j
e i)$. If the classes of the $u_i$ in $I/\mathfrak mI$ had a nontrivial $k$-linear relation, a coefficient different from zero could be solved for over the field $k$; consequently the other $n-1$ classes would span $I/\mathfrak mI$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to the finite $A$-module $I$, finite already from its displayed generating list. It would give $I=(u_j:j
e i)$, a contradiction. Thus these classes form a basis. This argument uses contraction for arbitrary monoid ideals, not merely principal ones.

The $p_i$ span $P^{\mathrm{gp}}\otimes\mathbf Q$, so $r\le n$. If $n=r$, these $n$ spanning vectors are a basis. The surjection $\mathbf N^n\to P$ sending the standard basis to $p_i$ is then injective: an equality of sums gives a rational linear relation on that basis, forcing equality of all integer coefficients. Thus $P\cong\mathbf N^r$. Conversely, a monoid isomorphism preserves indecomposable nonzero elements; in $\mathbf N^r$ they are exactly the $r$ standard basis vectors, so $P\cong\mathbf N^r$ implies $n=r$.

proof.text: Suppose $A$ is regular and put $d=\dim A$, $s=\dim(A/I)$. We have $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $I$ is proper, and its quotient is regular by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] to obtain parameters $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ and $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_c)$. The prefix-quotient assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] gives $s=d-c$ for exactly this parameter list. The assumed equality $d=s+r$ now gives $c=r$. Since the $c$ elements $x_i$ generate $I$, their classes span the vector space $I/\mathfrak mI$, whose basis in step 2 has size $n$. Hence $n\le c=r$; combine with $r\le n$ from step 3 to obtain $n=r$. Neither the number $c$ nor the quotient dimension is inferred from the kernel-parameters lemma alone.

Conversely suppose $n=r$. For any parameters $\bar b_1,\ldots,\bar b_s$ of $A/I$ and any lifts $b_i\in\mathfrak m$, the list $(u_1,\ldots,u_r,b_1,\ldots,b_s)$ generates $\mathfrak m$: reduce any $v\in\mathfrak m$ modulo $I$, express its image using the $\bar b_i$, lift the coefficients, and express the remaining element of $I$ using the $u_i$. Its length is $r+s=\dim A$, so [def-weil-regular-scheme] makes $A$ regular and [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters] makes this list a regular system of parameters. Under any chosen isomorphism $P\cong\mathbf N^r$, its basis maps to the indecomposables in some order, proving the assertion for the specified $t_i$. If $P=0$, all monoid lists are empty and $I=0$; if $r=0$, every $g\in P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ has zero image in its rationalization, so some positive integer kills $g$ (clear denominators in localization at the positive integers). Step 1 gives $g=0$, hence $P=0$ and $n=0$. If $s=0$, the parameter list downstairs is empty and the same generation argument gives $\mathfrak m=I$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q138-557530b64 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full; it has 5 steps and no new nodes. The statement is byte-identical to the base and to the live and side-live clones, where the item is still unsplit; there is no repair note and no SGA reference. Step 1: atoms are exactly a minimal generating set (cancellation + sharpness), and saturation applied to g and -g gives a torsion-free P^gp; this is elementary from def-trf-fs-log-blowup. Step 2: for J_i=∪_{j≠i}(p_j+P), contraction gives u_i∉(u_j:j≠i); the empty ideal covers n=1. Nakayama on the finitely generated module I then makes the classes a basis of I/mI. Step 3: r≤n, and n=r makes N^n→P injective; isomorphisms preserve atoms. Step 4: I⊆m is proper and A/I is regular, so kernel-parameters gives I=(x_1..x_c) and the generators-regular-sequence node gives s=d-c, hence c=r and n≤c=r≤n. Both cited statements say what is used. Step 5: lifting coefficients shows m is generated by u_i and b_j, which are dim A elements, so the definitions give A regular and a regular system of parameters. The edge cases P=0, r=0 (kernel of G→G⊗Q is torsion) and s=0 are covered. Source checks: ILO VI 1.2, 1.6 and 1.7 (pp. 69-70; VI 1.7 is Nizioł 5.2) and VIII 3.4.3. The item is a correctly labelled agent-written abstraction, and its hypotheses match exactly what parent lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary step 1 feeds into it. Small cases: k[[t]] with t gives a pass; with t^2 the hypothesis is excluded; k[[x^2,xy,y^2]] gives n=3>r=2, singular as predicted. lean.statement: theorem monoidal_local_regularity_criterion (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (P : Type v) [AddCommMonoid P] (hfs : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFineSaturatedMonoid (Multiplicative P)) (hsharp : ∀ p : P, IsAddUnit p → p = 0) (a : Multiplicative P →* A) (ha : ∀ p : P, p ≠ 0 → a (Multiplicative.ofAdd p) ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (hcontract : ∀ J : Set P, (∀ p ∈ J, ∀ q : P, p + q ∈ J) → ∀ p : P, a (Multiplicative.ofAdd p) ∈ Ideal.span ((fun q : P ↦ a (Multiplicative.ofAdd q)) '' J) ↔ p ∈ J) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I = Ideal.span ((fun p : P ↦ a (Multiplicative.ofAdd p)) '' {p | p ≠ 0})) (r : ℕ) (hr : r = Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup P)) [IsRegularLocalRing (A ⧸ I)] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = ringKrullDim (A ⧸ I) + (r : WithBot ℕ∞)) : {p : P | AddIrreducible p}.Finite ∧ AddSubmonoid.closure {p : P | AddIrreducible p} = ⊤ ∧ IsAddTorsionFree (Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup P) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (p : Fin n → P), Function.Injective p → Set.range p = {q : P | AddIrreducible q} → (∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin n) (A ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (I ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A I))), ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ x : I, (x : A) = a (Multiplicative.ofAdd (p i)) ∧ b i = Submodule.mkQ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A I)) x) ∧ (IsRegularLocalRing A ↔ n = r) ∧ (n = r ↔ Nonempty (P ≃+ (Fin r → ℕ)))) ∧ (∀ (e : P ≃+ (Fin r → ℕ)) (bs : List A), (∀ b ∈ bs, b ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) → IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (bs.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) → IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin r ↦ a (Multiplicative.ofAdd (e.symm (Pi.single i 1)))) ++ bs))
